extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, registered patent agents, IP practitioners, and patent office staff in India
extracted.subtask_description: Official Government of India notification amending the Patents Rules, 2003 (Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2024). Provides binding procedural requirements, timelines, forms, fee schedules, and processes for filing, examination, opposition, renewal, and other patent-office interactions in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to file statement and undertaking under section 8 (Form 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: In sub-rule (2), for the words ‘six months from the date of such filing’, the words ‘three months from the date of issuance of first statement of objections under sub-rule (3) of rule 24B or sub-rule (8) of rule 24C’ shall be substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must furnish the statement and undertaking required by section 8 within three months from issuance of the first statement of objections under the cited rules (i.e., timeline shortened from six months to three months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller may use accessible databases for foreign-filed application information
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Controller may, use accessible and available databases, for considering the information relating to applications filed in a country outside India.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may rely on public/accessible electronic databases to consider corresponding foreign-filed applications when assessing compliance with section 8; applicants should ensure foreign filing data is accurate and available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller may direct fresh Form 3 within two months
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Controller may, under sub-section (2) of section 8, for reasons to be recorded in writing, direct the applicant to furnish a fresh statement and undertaking in Form 3 within two months from the date of such communication by the Controller.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Controller finds the need, the applicant must provide an updated Form 3 within two months of the Controller’s written direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller may condone delay or extend time for filing Form 3 (up to 3 months) via Form 4
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, the Controller may condone the delay or extend the time for filing Form 3 for a period up to three months upon a request made in Form 4.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late filing of Form 3 can be condoned/extended for up to three months only upon a Form 4 request; applicants should file Form 4 and pay applicable fees per First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of further applications under section 16 (rule 13(2A))
rubrics_metrics.description: “(2A) A patent applicant may, if he so desires, file one or more further applications under section 16, including in respect of an invention disclosed in the provisional or complete specification or a further application filed under section 16.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules explicitly permit filing multiple divisional/further applications under section 16, including from provisional, complete or earlier further applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for making request for examination (rule 24B) reduced to 31 months
rubrics_metrics.description: In sub-rule (1), for the words ‘forty-eight months’, wherever they occur, the words ‘thirty-one months’ shall be substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time limit for filing a request for examination under section 11B (per rule 24B) is reduced from 48 to 31 months. A transitional clause (vi) preserves the old period for applications filed before commencement of these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provision for request-for-examination deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘(vi) Notwithstanding anything contained in this sub-rule, in respect of an application filed before commencement of the Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2024, the period for making request for examination under sub-section (1) of section 11B shall be the period specified under this sub-rule before the commencement of the Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2024.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed before the amendment continue to follow the earlier timeline for requesting examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period claim must be filed in Form 31 with fees (new rule 29A)
rubrics_metrics.description: “29A. Grace period. - An application to avail the period specified under section 31 shall be filed in Form 31, along with the fees specified in the First Schedule.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim the statutory grace period under section 31, applicants must submit Form 31 and pay the fee shown in the First Schedule; documentary evidence and undertakings required by Form 31 must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition/representation procedure and timelines (rule 55 sub-rule (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: “(3) On consideration of the representation if the Controller is satisfied that, - (a) no prima facie case is made out in the representation, he shall notify the opponent accordingly, and - (i) unless the opponent requests to be heard in the matter, the Controller shall, within one month from the date of such notification, pass an order recording the grounds for refusal of the representation; (ii) if opponent requests for a hearing, the Controller shall, after giving the opponent an opportunity of being heard, pass an order within one month from the date of hearing, recording his reasons for refusal or prima facie acceptance of the representation and the applicant shall be notified accordingly. (b) a prima facie case is made out in the representation, the Controller shall, within one month of receiving the representation, pass an order recording his reasons and notify the applicant accordingly.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Controller must act quickly (one-month timelines) to record reasons and pass orders on representations/oppositions; opponents can request hearings, in which case an order is still to be passed within one month of the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of certain time limits from three months to two months (rule 55 and rule 56 changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: In rule 55 sub-rule (4) and in rule 56 sub-rule (4), the word ‘three months’ is substituted with ‘two months’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific procedural response periods under rules 55 and 56 are shortened from three to two months (applicants/parties should check the precise sub-rules for which this applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing procedure for rule 55 to follow rule 62 (rule 55 sub-rule 5A)
rubrics_metrics.description: “(5A.) The procedure specified in sub-rules (2) to (4) of rule 62 shall, as far as may be, apply to the procedure for hearing under this rule.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing procedures under rule 55 should, as far as practicable, follow the procedures set out in rule 62(2)-(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications with representation to be examined under rule 24C (rule 55 sub-rule 5B)
rubrics_metrics.description: “(5B) An application for a patent, in which a representation for opposition has been filed and notice has been issued by the Controller under rule 3, shall be examined in accordance with rule 24C.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent applications facing representation/opposition will have their substantive examination proceed under rule 24C's procedures (which include timelines for statements of objections etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of inventorship (new rule 70A)
rubrics_metrics.description: “70A. Certificate of inventorship. - (1) The Controller may issue a certificate of inventorship to an inventor in respect of a patent in force, on a request made by the inventor in Form-8A along with fee specified in the First Schedule. (2) The Controller may issue a duplicate certificate of inventorship to an inventor in respect of a patent in force on a request made by the inventor in Form-8A along with the fee specified in the First Schedule and such request shall contain a statement setting out the circumstances in which the original certificate of inventorship was lost, destroyed, damaged or cannot be produced.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors may request certificates or duplicates in Form-8A and must provide reasons/circumstances for duplicate requests; fees apply as per the First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance payment of renewal fees and electronic discount (rule 80)
rubrics_metrics.description: “(3) The annual renewal fees payable in respect of two or more years may be paid in advance: Provided that where the renewal fees is paid in advance through electronic mode for a period of at least 4 years, a ten per cent reduction in fee shall be applicable for such renewal.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may pay multi-year renewals in advance; electronic advance payment for at least 4 years attracts a 10% discount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Designs Act and design specifications in rule 110 references
rubrics_metrics.description: In rule 110 sub-rule (2): for the words ‘Patents Act and Rules’, the words ‘The Patents Act, 1970 (39 of 1970), The Patents Rules, 2003, The Designs Act, 2000 (16 0f 2000) and The Designs Rules, 2001’ shall be substituted; and for the words ‘patent specifications’, the words ‘patent specifications, design specifications’ shall be substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References are broadened to include design legislation and design specifications where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic statement on working: frequency and filing window (rule 131)
rubrics_metrics.description: “(2) The statements referred to in sub-rule (1) shall be furnished once in respect of every period of three financial year, starting from the financial year commencing immediately after the financial year in which the patent was granted, and shall be furnished within six months from the expiry of each such period. Provided that the Controller may condone the delay or extend the time in filing of such statement for a period up to three months upon a request made in Form 4.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees/licensees must file working statements once every three financial years (starting after grant) within six months of period expiry; limited condonation (up to 3 months) via Form 4 is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions to applicability of certain procedural provisions (rule 137(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserted sub-rule (2) lists matters for which provisions of sub-rule (1) shall not be applicable, including: (i) extension of time or condonation of delay under sub-rule (5) of rule 12; (ii) clause (i) of sub-rule (4) and sub-rule (6) of rule 20; (iii) rule 21; (iv) sub-rules (1), (5) and (6) of rule 24B; (v) sub-rules (10) and (11) of rule 24C; (vi) sub-rule (4) of Rule 55; (vii) sub-rule (1A) of rule 80; (viii) sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 130; (ix) sub-rule(2) of rule 131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain matters are carved out from the general applicability of the provision being renumbered; practitioners should check the listed rules for their specific procedural regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller power to extend time or condone delay up to six months (rule 138)
rubrics_metrics.description: “138. Power to extend time specified or condone delay: - Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, the time specified for doing any act or taking any proceeding thereunder may be extended or any delay may be condoned by the Controller for a period of up to six months, upon a request made in Form 4, where such request is made before the expiry of the said period of six months: Provided that such request may be made any number of times within the specified period of six months.’.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller can extend or condone delays up to six months by Form 4 requests; multiple requests are permitted within that six-month window (practical limit of six months total unless earlier provisions provide otherwise).

rubrics_metrics.name: First Schedule (Table I) substituted — comprehensive fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: “In the said rules, for Table I of THE FIRST SCHEDULE, the following table shall be substituted, namely, - TABLE I …” (substituted table contains itemised fees for filing forms/actions: application fees, per-sheet/per-claim fees, sequence listing page fees, reductions for section 54 applications, fees for filing complete specification after provisional, fees for statement and undertaking under section 8, fees for requests for extension of time/condonation (per month), declaration as to inventorship, postdating, deletion of reference, claims under section 20, notices of opposition, requests for hearing, renewal fees by year, fees for amendments, certified copies, inspection, information requests, patent agent registration, transmittal fees for international applications, fees for preparation/transmission of certified priority documents, Form 27 (statement of working) — and many other entries with amounts specified for natural person/startup/small entity/educational institution and for other applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The First Schedule replaces the entire fee matrix for a very large number of patent office transactions. Practitioners must consult the substituted Table I for the exact fee amounts applicable to each form/entry/action (the Gazette reproduces the detailed numeric amounts and caps for multiple-priority cases and per-page charges). Key features include per-sheet and per-claim extra fees, a 50% reduction for section 54 applications in some items, and differentiated fees for 'natural person/startup/small entity/educational institution' versus 'other(s)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees-related specific rules: per-sheet, per-claim, sequence-listing charges and section 54 reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Table I entries: On application for a patent under sections 7, 54* or 135 and rule 20(1) accompanied by provisional or complete specification— (i) for each sheet of specification in addition to 30, excluding sequence listing of nucleotides and/or amino acid sequences under sub-rule (3) of rule (9); (ii) for each claim in addition to 10; (iii) for each page of sequence listing of nucleotides and/or amino acid sequences under sub-rule (3) of rule (9). *An application for a patent made under section 54 shall be eligible for a reduction of 50 per cent in fee as compared to other applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing and filing specifications, applicants must account for extra fees for sheets beyond 30, extra claims beyond 10, and sequence listing pages; section 54 applications may receive a 50% fee reduction where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form mapping updates in THE SECOND SCHEDULE (Forms list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in the Second Schedule are changed: the entry corresponding to 'Form-4' is substituted to read: '4. Sections 53(2) and 142(4), rules 12(5), 13(6), 24B(6), 24C(11), 80(1A), 130 and 138. Request for extension of time or condonation of delay.' After Form-8, new Form 8A (Rule 70A Certificate of inventorship) is added. After Form-30, Form 31 (Section 31 and rule 29A Grace period) is inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Second Schedule's list of forms and their statutory/regulatory bases is updated; practitioners must use the renumbered/inserted forms for the specified purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 1 (Application for grant of patent) content and required attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituted Form 1 (Application for grant of patent) sets out required fields (applicant reference, type of application — ordinary/convention/PCT-NP/PPH/divisional/patent of addition, applicant(s) and inventor(s details including optional demographic fields, category of applicant e.g., natural person/startup/small entity/educational institution, title of invention, authorised registered patent agent, address for service, particulars for convention/PCT/divisional/patent of addition, detailed declarations including declaration of inventorship and that provisional/complete specification is filed, and a checklist of attachments). Attachments enumerated include Form 2, complete/provisional specification, sequence listing (electronic), drawings, priority documents or DAS retrieval request, translations, Form 3 (statement & undertaking), Form 5 (declaration of inventorship), power of authority, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must populate all prescribed fields, tick applicable boxes, provide declarations and submit the listed attachments; some fields require OTP-verified contact details (to be redacted). Fee per First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 3 (Statement and undertaking under section 8) content and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituted Form 3 provides the format for the statement and undertaking under section 8: applicant(s) must declare whether corresponding foreign applications exist (or not), list particulars (country, date, application number, status, publication/disposal dates), name and address of assignee (if any), and undertake to keep the Controller informed in writing regarding details of corresponding applications filed outside India until grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 3 must be signed by the applicant or authorized patent agent. Where foreign filings exist, full particulars must be given; where none exist, the applicant must state that fact. The undertaking to update the Controller until grant is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 4 (Request for extension of time or condonation of delay) content and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituted Form 4 (Request for extension of time or condonation of delay) requires the name of applicant, signature by applicant or authorized registered patent agent, name of the natural person who has signed, particulars of the extension requested (number of months, statutory provision), connection to application/patent number, and the reasons for making the request. Note: For fee: See First Schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 4 must set out reasons for condonation/extension; fee and timing requirements (must be made before expiry of the relevant period as per rule 138) must be complied with. Filing a Form 4 does not guarantee grant of condonation; Controller has discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8A (Certificate of Inventorship) content and mandatory fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8A requests issuance/duplicate issuance of a 'Certificate of Inventorship' and requires inventor name, patent number, signature, date, and mandatorily for Indian inventors the Aadhaar number and contact/address details; for duplicate requests a statement setting out circumstances in which original certificate was lost/destroyed/damaged/unavailable must be provided. Note: 'This Certificate does not, in any manner whatsoever, confer or derogate from any rights under the patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 8A must contain mandatory identity information for Indian inventors; fees as per First Schedule apply. The certificate is administrative and does not alter patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 27 (Statement regarding working of patented invention on commercial scale) obligations and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituted Form 27 requires the patentee/licensee to insert name, address, nationality, patent numbers, financial year to which statement relates, indicate whether each patent is 'Worked' or 'Not worked', and if 'Not worked' to tick appropriate reasons (under development, under commercial trial, review/approval with regulatory authorities, etc.), whether patent is available for licensing, and optionally provide contact details for license enquiries. Notes include: one form may be filed for multiple related patents granted to same patentee(s); subject to conditions a patent is not 'not worked' solely because the product was imported into India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every patentee and licensee must file this statement as required; truthful declarations and accurate reasons are mandatory. The form clarifies that importation alone doesn't necessarily mean 'not worked'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 31 (Grace period claim) content and documentary evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 31 (Grace Period) requires applicant details, application number, applicable section 31(a)-(d) provision(s), documentary evidence for earliest date(s) of display/use/publication and whether display occurred with consent of true & first inventor (or without consent where relevant), and an undertaking that the invention was in the public domain from the stated date and that the application is made within 12 months from that date. Note: Affidavit, if any, shall be signed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim the grace period the applicant must supply documentary evidence and undertakings; the claim must be made within 12 months from the earliest public disclosure/use/publication as relevant to the section 31 limb invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: THE FOURTH SCHEDULE substituted — costs to be awarded in proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: THE FOURTH SCHEDULE (proviso to rule 136(1)) is substituted to list matters in respect of which costs may be awarded and the amounts (in rupees) for 'Natural person(s) or Startup(s) or Small entit(y)/ educational institution(s)' and for 'Other(s)'. Entries include costs for notice of opposition under various sections, applications for compulsory licence, application for revision of terms and conditions of licence, notice of intention to attend hearing, stamp fees for powers of attorney/affidavits, fees for written statements/replies/affidavits, charges for each publication/document produced, unnecessary affidavits/citations, per day hearing costs, and an aggregate/twice-aggregate rule for sub-rule (2) of rule 136, among others (with amounts specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fourth Schedule prescribes recoverable costs for a variety of contested proceedings; amounts differ by applicant category. Parties should be aware that costs can be awarded and are quantified in the Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFTH SCHEDULE headings updated to reflect applicant categories
rubrics_metrics.description: In the FIFTH SCHEDULE, headings are substituted to read: include columns for 'Natural person(s) or Startup(s) or Small entit(y)/ (ies) or educational institution(s)' and 'Other(s), alone or with natural person(s) or Startup(s) or Small entit(y)/ (ies) or educational institution(s)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule headings clarify fee/cost categories to distinguish reduced fees for natural persons/startups/small entities/educational institutions from other applicants.
